query: Which proxy data sources and contractual/legal arrangements can substitute for proprietary sales or retailer inventories to measure consumption shifts?

response.query: Which proxy data sources and contractual/legal arrangements can substitute for proprietary sales or retailer inventories to measure consumption shifts?
response.answer: Proxy data sources include industry reports and market research firms. Contractual/legal arrangements involve third-party data sharing agreements and government databases. These substitute for proprietary sales or retailer inventories to measure consumption shifts.

results.title: IPAY 2028 Final Guidance
results.content: To determine the ceiling for renegotiation, CMS will maintain the underlying data that was used to calculate the amounts considered for the ceiling at the time of negotiation in accordance with section 1194(c) of the Act but will make the following adjustments to the calculations: (1) incorporate Part B data in accordance with sections 60.2.1, 60.2.2.3, and 60.2.3 of this final guidance, as applicable (i.e., for selected drugs for initial price applicability years 2026 and 2027 that are also payable under Part B and selected for renegotiation); (2) update the applicable percent applied to the average non-FAMP amount(s) to reflect the appropriate monopoly status with respect to the initial price applicability year for which an agreed-upon MFP after renegotiation will apply (i.e., initial price applicability year 2028), as applicable; and (3) adjust the amounts considered for the ceiling (i.e., the sum of the plan-specific enrollment amounts and the average non-FAMP amount) for inflation (percent increase in CPI-U as explained below).

results.title: FAQs
results.content: In light of the SEC’s recent exemptive order, there are new dates by which Large Industry Members (which are Industry Members other than Small Industry Members) are required to begin reporting to the CAT. Large Industry Members are required to begin reporting Phase 2a Industry Member Data to the CAT by June 22, 2020, and are required to begin reporting Phase 2b Industry Member Data to the CAT by July 20, 2020. •    Small Industry Members that are required to record or report information to FINRA’s Order Audit Trail System pursuant to applicable SRO rules (referred to as “Small Industry OATS Reporters”) are required to begin reporting Phase 2a Industry Member Data to the CAT by June 22, 2020. •    Small Industry Members that are not required to record or report information to FINRA’s Order Audit Trail System pursuant to applicable SRO rules (referred to as “Small Industry Non-OATS Reporters”) are required to begin reporting Phase 2a Industry Member Data to the CAT by December 13, 2021.
